text: Outdoor agricultural work can create heat stress risk. Consider temperature, humidity, air movement, physical workload, clothing/PPE, duration and breaks. Use hydration, rest and scheduling controls appropriate to the work and local guidance.
Pesticide work should follow the product label and SDS. Assess chemical hazard, exposure routes, required PPE, equipment condition, weather and drift controls before spraying.
Weather-sensitive tasks should be reassessed when conditions change. Wind can affect spray drift, rain can affect outdoor work and treatment effectiveness, and high heat can increase worker exposure.
Missing critical safety information should not be treated as low risk. If the chemical identity, label/SDS or required PPE cannot be verified, the system should flag the assessment as incomplete.
